title: Destructuring
summary: Destructuring is syntax for unpacking values from arrays or properties from objects into individual variables. It appears in every React component (props), every hook call (useState, useEffect return values), and every API response. Object destructuring matches by property name; array destructuring matches by position. You can rename variables, provide default values, nest destructuring, and skip elements.
keyPoints: Object destructuring: const { title, year } = movie — matches by property name
Array destructuring: const [first, second] = arr — matches by position
Rename while destructuring: const { title: movieTitle } = movie
Default values: const { tagline = 'No tagline' } = movie
Nested destructuring: const { director: { name } } = movie — director is NOT extracted as a variable
Skip array elements: const [first, , third] = arr
Destructure in function parameters: function Card({ title, rating }) {}
useState returns a two-element array: const [count, setCount] = useState(0)

exercises.explanation: Object destructuring uses {} and matches by property name. Array destructuring uses [] and matches by position — objects are not arrays.
Nested destructuring goes into director and extracts name. Note: director is NOT declared as a variable here — only name is.

exercises.prompt:
Given:
const genres = ['Action', 'Sci-Fi', 'Thriller']

How do you skip 'Sci-Fi' and get only 'Action' and 'Thriller'?
exercises.explanation: An empty slot (consecutive commas with nothing between) skips that position in array destructuring.

exercises.prompt: A React component is called as <MovieCard title="Inception" rating={8.8} />. Which function signature correctly destructures the props?
exercises.explanation: React passes all props as a single object. Destructuring in the parameter list is the idiomatic way to pull out individual props.

exercises.prompt:
Given:
const movie = { title: 'Unknown' }
const { title: movieTitle, tagline = 'No tagline' } = movie

What are the values of movieTitle and tagline?
exercises.explanation: title is renamed to movieTitle and gets the value 'Unknown'. tagline does not exist on movie, so it falls back to the default 'No tagline'.

exercises.prompt:
const [count, setCount] = useState(0)

Why is array destructuring used here instead of object destructuring?
options: useState returns an array, so you use [] to destructure it
Object destructuring does not work with hooks
React requires [] syntax for all hooks
exercises.answer: useState returns an array, so you use [] to destructure it
exercises.explanation: useState returns [currentValue, setter]. Because it's an array, you destructure with []. The advantage is you can name the variables whatever you like — count and setCount are your choice.
